target_customer: Electrical engineers, students, educators and hobbyists; universities and subscribers
problem: Circuit simulation tools were expensive desktop software that did not run well on Macs. CircuitLab runs schematic capture and simulation in the browser.
business_model: freemium SaaS subscription (free at launch; revenue model not described in 2013 coverage)
product_category: online circuit simulator and schematic editor

founders.name: Mike Robbins
previous_startups: Pantelligent (earlier name per a search listing)
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page and TechCrunch 2013-03-18.

founders.name: Humberto Evans
founders.background_notes: YC page profile; named by TechCrunch 2013-03-18.

competitors.name: Upverter
competitors.what: Web based electronics design and PCB tool aimed at professionals
competitors.traction_then: 17,000 parts and thousands of public designs; adoption starting among startup professionals

competitors.name: Circuits.io
competitors.what: Browser circuit and board design aimed at students and hobbyists

competitors.name: PartSim
competitors.what: Free login free simulator on ngspice from Aspen Labs and DigiKey

technical_complexity.rationale: Accurate SPICE class analog simulation and a schematic editor running in a browser with JavaScript in 2012 was hard for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: A custom simulator is hard to copy quickly, and classes and saved designs create lock in, but free rivals existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows incumbents buying or copying CircuitLab; DigiKey launched PartSim and Scheme-It separately. CircuitLab remains independent.

market_need_then: TechCrunch March 2013 reports about 70,000 monthly users, strongest in academia, and an Electronic Design article reports over 500 colleges and 80,000 simulations a week.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and technical, with playful blog posts including an April 1 Circuit-oids game post.

branding.community_and_virality: Embedded as the schematic tool on Electronics.StackExchange.com and a partnership with UBM Tech (TechCrunch 2013); Slashdot and Hacker News covered the 2012 launch.

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive but credible name with distribution through StackExchange and EE publishers, though no independent brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: CircuitLab launched publicly in February 2012, reached 70,000 monthly users within a year through StackExchange and academic adoption, and joined YC in Winter 2013 with a small seed. It remains an independent two person style business and now ships an AI assistant, so it looks like a durable niche tool rather than a venture scale outcome; no exit found.
notes: The CircuitLab about page named no founders. CB Insights lists a 0.5M convertible note on 2013-03-27 with Steve Blank, aggregator only, not recorded; the Xconomy 100K seed is one outlet and cross-checked only against the aggregator. An earlier name Pantelligent appears on a FundersClub listing, seen only in a search summary. An April 1 2012 'Circuit-oids' post is likely a joke, not a pivot. Outcome search found no acquisition, layoffs or shutdown. Rival Upverter had unrelated later outcomes, not recorded.
